topic: Sections of a Cone and the Circle
title: One Cone, 4 Curves? Conic Sections Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Slice an ice cream cone straight across and you get a circle. Tilt the knife and you get an oval, tilt it more and the curve never closes, cut straight down and you get yet another curve. How can one cone hide four curves? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 10, Conic Sections) we meet all four conic sections and then the first one, the circle.

You will watch a double cone being built from two sticks, then tilt a cutting plane live while the angle beta counts down and the slice morphs from a circle to an ellipse, a parabola and a hyperbola. A compass traces a circle while the distance from the centre stays fixed, and we derive (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² step by step from a right triangle. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with completing the square, the exam trap about adding to both sides, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
